items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I went to Cleveland to play with a trumpeter whose name was John Wilson... Little John liked my playing and wanted me to play with his band

ctx.x: Now from Detroit did you -- as a piano player -- did you venture out like to Toledo or wherever from Detroit? Did you do some run-outs?

At one time I went to Cleveland to play with a trumpeter whose name was John Wilson. He’s short in stature, so he called himself Little John, and he called his band the Merry Men. Little John and his Merry Men. We played a theater in Cleveland for about a week called the Globe Theater. There I met -- there was a singer and a comedian on the show. I had had -- I was not in possession of an instrument. I didn’t own an instrument, because all mine had been stolen. Little John liked my playing and wanted me to play…
We asked this about Cincinnati. Did you think of Detroit as having a sound? If so, how would you characterize it, at least for the scene that you were involved, which was the bebop?
